articles.title: Mulher que desapareceu em pescaria com o marido é acha morta em SC | G1
articles.standfirst: Roselene Assunção, de 64 anos, foi achada neste domingo (1º). Marido dela, Paulo Assunção, de 63 anos, foi localizado morto no sábado (31).
articles.summary: Roselene Assunção, de 64 anos, foi achada neste domingo (1º). Marido dela, Paulo Assunção, de 63 anos, foi localizado morto no sábado (31).
articles.body:
Casal é achado após desaparecer ao sair para pescar em São José — Foto: Reprodução Arquidiocese de Florianópolis/CBMSC

Os bombeiros encontraram, neste domingo (1º), o corpo de Roselene Assunção , de 64 anos. Ela estava desaparecida desde sexta-feira (30), quando saiu para pescar com o marido em São José (SC). O marido dela, Paulo Assunção , de 63 anos, foi localizado morto no sábado (31).

Roselene foi encontrada perto das ilhas Ratones Grande e Ratones Pequeno, em Florianópolis , com o apoio de um helicóptero do Serviço de Atendimento e Resgate Aeromédico (SARC).

Após o resgate, a equipe levou o corpo para o Grupamento de Busca e Salvamento (GBS), localizado na região da Ponte Hercílio Luz, área central da cidade.

A Polícia Civil foi acionada para iniciar os trabalhos de perícia e encaminhar o corpo ao Instituto Médico Legal (IML).

Paulo era irmão do padre João Assunção, e Roselene, cunhada do religioso. Em nota, a Arquidiocese de Florianópolis lamentou a morte do casal.

"A Arquidiocese, na esperança da vida eterna, reza pelo descanso de sua alma e pede a Deus que conforte os corações de seus amigos e familiares", escreveu.

As buscas começaram depois que familiares informaram que o casal saiu para pescar nas proximidades das Pedras da Tipininga, em São José, na noite de sexta-feira, e não voltou.

No sábado (31), as equipes de resgate localizaram o corpo de Paulo e o barco do casal, que estava parcialmente submerso.

A força-tarefa usou embarcações e equipamentos tecnológicos para ampliar a área de buscas e ajudar na localização das vítimas.

articles.title: VÍDEO: acidente de avião no Amazonas deixa três feridos na BR-230 | G1
articles.standfirst: Imagens mostram aeronave com o bico voltado para o chão; três pessoas da mesma família ficaram feridas, entre elas uma criança de 5 anos e uma mulher grávida.
articles.summary: O acidente de avião no Amazonas ocorreu na Transamazônica, deixando uma criança em estado grave e uma gestante ferida após a aeronave cair e virar em área de mata.
articles.body:
Um avião de pequeno porte ficou virado de cabeça para baixo após sofrer um acidente na manhã deste domingo (1º), na rodovia Transamazônica (BR-230) , entre Humaitá e Apuí, no interior do Amazonas. Três pessoas que estavam a bordo ficaram feridas, entre elas uma criança de 5 anos e uma mulher grávida.

Imagens compartilhadas nas redes sociais mostram a aeronave com o bico voltado para o chão, em uma área de mata às margens da pista de barro. Segundo testemunhas, o avião estaria decolando no momento do acidente. Os ocupantes seriam da mesma família.

Entre as vítimas estão Marcela Pereira Pinheiro, de 35 anos, grávida de aproximadamente nove semanas; Beatriz Pinheiro Fagundes, de 5 anos, que ficou em estado grave; e Elson Fagundes de Oliveira, de 45 anos. Não houve mortes.

Segundo informações repassadas pelo Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Amazonas (CBMAM), a criança sofreu uma ruptura no diafragma, com deslocamento do fígado. Elson teve um corte profundo na testa. Marcela não apresentava lesões aparentes e permaneceu em atendimento e acompanhamento psicológico.

Os ocupantes foram retirados do local por motoristas que passavam pela rodovia e começaram a ser transportados em um veículo particular para Humaitá.

A equipe do Hospital Municipal encontrou as vítimas nas proximidades da balsa e assumiu o transporte até a unidade de saúde. Os bombeiros também foram acionados para prestar apoio, mas não precisaram atuar diretamente na ocorrência.

Ainda conforme os bombeiros, a aeronave não apresentava vazamento de combustível e não oferecia risco imediato que exigisse intervenção da equipe no local.

A Força Aérea Brasileira (FAB) informou que investigadores do Centro de Investigação e Prevenção de Acidentes Aeronáuticos (Cenipa) foram acionados neste domingo para investigar a ocorrência com a aeronave de matrícula PU-BLR, em Humaitá.

A equipe do Sétimo Serviço Regional de Investigação e Prevenção de Acidentes Aeronáuticos (Seripa VII), com sede em Manaus, realizou a chamada Ação Inicial, etapa em que são coletados dados, preservados elementos e verificados os danos causados à aeronave.

Segundo a FAB, as informações levantadas vão subsidiar a investigação. As causas do acidente ainda não foram divulgadas.

articles.title: Médico Júlio César Barreto morre em Goiânia | G1
articles.standfirst: Morte causou comoção na comunidade médica e entre pacientes em Goiás. O nefrologista integrava a equipe de transplantes do HGG.
articles.summary: Morte causou comoção na comunidade médica e entre pacientes em Goiás. O nefrologista integrava a equipe de transplantes do HGG.
articles.body:
Médico Júlio César Soares Barreto morre em Goiânia — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram de TRS Nefrologia e hemodiálise

A morte do médico nefrologista Júlio César Soares Barreto, de 57 anos, causou comoção na comunidade médica em Goiás. O médico fazia parte da equipe de transplantes do Hospital Estadual Dr. Alberto Rassi (HGG), que lamentou profundamente a partida em uma nota de pesar. A causa da morte não foi divulgada.

Júlio César morreu neste sábado (31), em Goiânia . Segundo um texto compartilhado pela família, o médico dedicou sua vida a salvar vidas, "fazendo do transplante uma missão de amor e esperança". Neste mesmo texto, a família informa que os órgãos do médico devem ser doados.

"Partiu dessa vida, mas continuará vivendo em outras vidas. Seu exemplo de amor ao próximo será eterno nos nossos corações", diz a homenagem.

Diferentes instituições da Saúde também publicaram notas de pesar, como o Hospital São Lucas de Goiânia, do qual Júlio César era sócio. "Sua dedicação à medicina e o cuidado com cada paciente marcaram todos que tiveram a oportunidade de conviver com ele" , diz a nota.

A Sociedade Brasileira de Nefrologia também lamentou a morte do nefrologista, destacando sua trajetória profissional.

"Ao longo de sua trajetória profissional, Júlio César Barreto dedicou-se à Nefrologia, contribuindo de maneira significativa para a formação de diversos nefrologistas no estado de Goiás, deixando um importante legado de conhecimento, dedicação ao ensino e compromisso com a especialidade".

Amigos, colegas de profissão, pacientes e familiares de pacientes também publicaram homenagens. "Vou sentir falta das suas piadocas, da sua inteligência inigualável e, principalmente, das inúmeras histórias que você sempre tinha para contar. Cada conversa era uma aula, uma oportunidade de aprender alguma coisa nova" , diz uma delas.

"Minha eterna gratidão ao Dr. Júlio, que cuidou com tanta dedicação da minha família. Obrigada por transformar conhecimento em cuidado, profissão em missão e tantas vidas em um legado de amor", escreveu outra.

O velório está marcado para esta segunda-feira (2), das 8h às 17h, no Parque Memorial de Goiânia.

Veja o que abre e fecha no feriado de Finados na Baixada Santista — Foto: Alexsander Ferrat/AT

articles.title: Ataque a tiros deixa dois mortos no bairro São Jorge, em BH | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a PM, dupla foi alvo de disparos feitos por ocupantes de um carro, que fugiram após o ataque; vítimas chegaram a ser socorridas, mas morreram no hospital.
articles.summary: Segundo a PM, dupla foi alvo de disparos feitos por ocupantes de um carro, que fugiram após o ataque; vítimas chegaram a ser socorridas, mas morreram no hospital.
articles.body:
Sirene Polícia Militar — Foto: Reprodução Google

Dois homens, de 25 e 26 anos, morreram após serem baleados na noite deste sábado (31), no bairro São Jorge I, na região Oeste de Belo Horizonte .

Segundo relatos de populares à Polícia Militar, houve diversos disparos em direção à dupla vindos de ocupantes de um carro sedan que, em seguida, fugiu. A informação de que os baleados teriam envolvimento com o tráfico de drogas e envolvimento com o Terceiro Comando Puro (TCP) também foi repassada aos militares.

Uma das vítimas foi socorrida por moradores e levada para a UPA Oeste. A outra, conseguiu correr para uma rua próxima e foi encontrada caída pela Polícia Militar, ainda com vida. Ela foi encaminhada ao Hospital João XXIII, acompanhada pela mãe em uma viatura.

Os homens chegaram a receber atendimento médico, mas não resistiram aos ferimentos.

Em nota, a Polícia Civil de Minas Gerais (PCMG) informou ao g1 que a perícia oficial esteve no local do crimee realizou os trabalhos de praxe.

Até o momento, ninguém foi conduzido à Delegacia de Plantão. Os suspeitos e o veículo usado no crime ainda não foram localizados.

articles.title: Médico bêbado é preso por ameaçar vendedor de bar com uma arma no ES | G1
articles.standfirst: Policiais foram abordados por outros clientes que informaram sobre a confusão no estabelecimento. Médico foi autuado em flagrante por ameaça e porte ilegal de arma.
articles.summary: Policiais foram abordados por outros clientes que informaram sobre a confusão no estabelecimento. Médico foi autuado em flagrante por ameaça e porte ilegal de arma.
articles.body:
Médico Marcio Antonio Leite Lima, de 57 anos, foi preso após ameaçar um vendedor de uma distribuidora — Foto: Reprodução

Um médico de 57 anos foi preso em flagrante após ameaçar um vendedor de uma distribuidora de bebidas com uma arma na tarde deste sábado (31), na Avenida Hugo Musso, no bairro Praia da Costa, em Vila Velha , na Grande Vitória.

Segundo a Guarda Municipal, Marcio Antonio Leite Lima apresentava sinais de embriaguez e estava armado com um revólver calibre 38.

De acordo com a Guarda Municipal, agentes passavam pela avenida quando foram chamados por pessoas que estavam perto da distribuidora. Elas informaram que um homem armado discutia e ameaçava um vendedor do estabelecimento.

Os guardas abordaram o suspeito e, durante a revista, encontraram um revólver da marca Taurus, calibre 38, no bolso dele.

O homem foi levado à Delegacia Regional de Vila Velha e autuado em flagrante pelos crimes de ameaça e porte ilegal de arma de fogo de uso permitido.

Segundo a Polícia Civil, após a autuação, ele foi encaminhado ao Centro de Triagem, em Viana.

A Secretaria de Estado da Saúde (Sesa) informou que o médico teve vínculo temporário com o Hospital Estadual Dr. Dório Silva, entre abril de 2010 e abril de 2011, mas está desligado da unidade desde então.

articles.title: Comprimido diário tem resultado inédito no câncer que mais mata | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa recente conseguiu um resultado inédito em que mais da metade dos pacientes com câncer de pulmão avançado ficou sete anos sem a doença progredir. De acordo com especialistas, tratamento muda panorama da doença, mas ainda há dificuldade no acesso.
articles.summary: Pesquisa recente conseguiu um resultado inédito em que mais da metade dos pacientes com câncer de pulmão avançado ficou sete anos sem a doença progredir. De acordo com especialista
articles.body:
Antes e depois de três meses do tratamento com medicamento para câncer de pulmão — Foto: Divulgação

Durante décadas, o diagnóstico de câncer de pulmão avançado equivalia, na prática, a uma sentença de meses. Hoje, um comprimido tomado uma vez ao dia está mudando essa conta. Uma pesquisa recente conseguiu um resultado inédito: mais da metade dos pacientes com câncer de pulmão avançado ficou sete anos sem a doença progredir.

A pesquisa acompanhou pacientes com câncer de pulmão avançado usando lorlatinibe, medicamento tomado diariamente em forma de comprimido. Após sete anos de acompanhamento, 55% dos pacientes permaneceram vivos e sem progressão da doença — um resultado inédito para uma doença avançada.

🔴 O lorlatinibe não é para qualquer paciente com câncer de pulmão. Ele funciona apenas em casos em que o tumor é impulsionado por uma alteração genética específica chamada rearranjo de ALK. Essa alteração está presente em cerca de 3% a 7% dos casos do tipo mais comum de câncer de pulmão.

Embora represente uma parcela pequena dos casos, o avanço chama atenção porque o câncer de pulmão continua sendo o que mais mata homens e mulheres no país, com 31.237 mortes por ano, segundo o Instituto Nacional de Câncer (INCA).

Uma delas é Paula Piteri, que descobriu a doença aos 38 anos, com três filhos e sonhos pela frente. Hoje, ela usa o lorlatinibe há quase um ano e afirma que recuperou algo que o diagnóstico parecia ter tirado: a perspectiva de futuro. (Leia mais abaixo)

🔴 Mas o entusiasmo com os dados científicos esbarra em um problema: o medicamento é de alto custo, cerca de R$ 37 mil por mês pelos comprimidos, e não está no Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS). Quem tem acesso hoje tem cobertura de plano de saúde, conseguiu na Justiça pelo SUS ou pagou.

Câncer de pulmão é o que mais mata homens e mulheres no Brasil — Foto: Freepik

Uma terapia feita para um alvo específico

O lorlatinibe é um exemplo do que os oncologistas chamam de terapia-alvo: medicamentos desenvolvidos para atacar alterações genéticas específicas que fazem um tumor crescer.

Essa estratégia representa uma mudança importante na forma de tratar o câncer. Durante décadas, os tratamentos eram definidos principalmente pelo órgão afetado — câncer de pulmão recebia um protocolo, câncer de mama outro. Hoje, exames genéticos conseguem identificar quais mutações estão impulsionando o crescimento de cada tumor.

Com essa informação, os médicos podem escolher medicamentos desenhados para bloquear exatamente o mecanismo que mantém aquelas células cancerosas ativas. O lorlatinibe é um desses casos: ele não é indicado para todos os pacientes com câncer de pulmão, mas para um subtipo específico da doença que apresenta uma alteração no gene ALK.

Em cerca de 3% a 5% dos casos de câncer de pulmão de não pequenas células, ocorre um rearranjo no gene ALK. Essa alteração faz com que a célula passe a produzir uma proteína defeituosa que envia sinais contínuos de crescimento e multiplicação, funcionando como um interruptor permanentemente ligado.

O lorlatinibe foi desenvolvido para bloquear essa proteína. Ao se ligar ao alvo molecular, o medicamento interrompe o sinal que estimula a proliferação das células tumorais.

O medicamento foi projetado para superar duas limitações observadas em gerações anteriores de medicamentos contra ALK: a resistência que o tumor desenvolve ao longo do tempo e a dificuldade de atingir o cérebro.

Essa última característica é especialmente importante porque as metástases cerebrais estão entre as complicações mais frequentes desse tipo de câncer avançado. Entre 25% e 40% dos pacientes podem desenvolver tumores no cérebro dois anos depois do diagnóstico.

O lorlatinibe consegue atravessar a barreira hematoencefálica — um sistema de proteção natural que impede a entrada de muitas substâncias no cérebro e que também dificulta a ação de diversos medicamentos.

O medicamento já é aprovado e utilizado na prática clínica. Os novos dados apresentados agora ampliam o tempo de acompanhamento dos pacientes e ajudam a entender por quanto tempo o controle da doença pode ser mantido.

E foi aí que os resultados impressionaram os médicos: mesmo após sete anos de acompanhamento, mais da metade dos pacientes seguia com a doença controlada.

Para os especialistas, o resultado muda a pergunta quando um paciente tem o diagnóstico: não é mais quanto tempo o paciente tem, mas qual é minha chance de viver muitos anos com a doença controlada?

Segundo o oncologista Gustavo Schvartsman, do Hospital Sírio-Libanês, o ganho observado é resultado de uma evolução gradual dessas terapias.

"Nunca alguém passava de cinco anos sem a doença progredir quando só existia quimioterapia. Com os inibidores de primeira geração, foi para 5% ou 10% dos pacientes; com a segunda geração, 20% a 30%; agora chegamos a 55%. O avanço é muito grande e vemos um passo enorme no dia a dia do paciente", afirma.

Paula Piteri tinha 38 anos quando descobriu, em 2020, que um nódulo no pulmão era câncer. Ela conta que tinha sido mãe há pouco tempo e que queria fazer cirurgia plástica. Levando uma vida saudável, sem qualquer histórico de cigarro, ela foi fazer um exame de rotina quando descobriu a doença.

No primeiro diagnóstico, Paula não fez um sequenciamento genético. Retirou o tumor e achou que, depois da cirurgia, estaria livre. No entanto, em 2025 recebeu o novo diagnóstico: o câncer tinha voltado.

“Foi um choque, eu sou mãe de três crianças e isso podia mudar minha vida completamente”, conta.

Hoje, ela usa o lorlatinibe, fornecido pelo plano de saúde. O medicamento está na lista da Agência Nacional de Saúde Suplementar (ANS) e, com isso, os planos são obrigados a fornecê-lo.

“É muito bom ter perspectiva, saber que eu tenho vida para viver. Eu quero fazer parte disso e viver por muitos anos ainda”, diz.

O que os 7 anos de dados revelam e o que ainda falta saber

Sete anos de acompanhamento é um número raro em oncologia, e quem pesquisa câncer reconhece o peso disso. Para o oncologista Stephen Stefani, o dado precisa ser lido dentro de uma trajetória histórica: quando só havia quimioterapia, nenhum paciente com esse diagnóstico chegava a cinco anos sem progressão. Os inibidores de cada geração foram ampliando esse horizonte.

"A diferença de eficácia se torna muito gritante quando você vê essa análise de sete anos e é um resultado relevante para o paciente", avalia.

Matheus Henrique Dias, biomédico e especialista em biologia molecular que pesquisa medicamentos para o tratamento do câncer na Holanda, também diz que o estudo tem avanços promissores.

"Para quem tem essa mutação específica, vai ser de fato uma mudança grande", diz.

🔴 Mas ambos levantam pontos que os dados ainda não respondem. No estudo, 45% dos pacientes não tiveram sucesso e ainda é preciso entender por que a terapia não funciona para eles.

Outro ponto que Stephen e Matheus comentam é que há efeitos colaterais. Ao todo, 52% dos pacientes relataram algum efeito no sistema nervoso central: alterações cognitivas, mudanças de humor e, em menor frequência, impactos psiquiátricos mais graves. No total, eventos adversos de grau 3 ou 4 — que são os mais graves, com impacto no dia a dia — ocorreram em 77% dos pacientes.

"A gente vê que ainda há alguns pontos que precisam ser considerados. É importante que as pessoas vivam, mas é muito importante que elas continuem sendo, em boa medida, elas mesmas", diz Dias.

Medicamento ainda não está disponível no SUS — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

Antes mesmo do tratamento, há um obstáculo menos visível: o diagnóstico molecular. Identificar a mutação de ALK exige testes genéticos que, em muitos casos, não estão disponíveis, nem mesmo com planos de saúde.

"Não adianta fazer o teste num sistema onde o remédio não vai estar disponível. E não adianta ter o remédio se o paciente não conseguiu o diagnóstico correto", resume Schvartsman.

E ainda há a barreira de acesso ao medicamento. Hoje, de acordo com a tabela de preços definida pelo Ministério da Saúde, o medicamento tem preço máximo de R$ 37 mil a caixa com 30 comprimidos.

Mantido por sete anos, período observado no estudo, o tratamento ultrapassaria R$ 3,1 milhões por paciente.

O medicamento chegou a ser debatido na Comissão Nacional de Incorporação de Tecnologias no Sistema Único de Saúde (Conitec), porém não foi aprovado por causa do alto custo para o Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS).

“O Comitê de Medicamentos considerou que, apesar das evidências apresentadas e dos benefícios do tratamento, a relação de custo-efetividade não aponta eficiência para o SUS, tendo em vista que nenhuma das intervenções ficou abaixo do limite de custo-efetividade”, pontuou a comissão no relatório.

O g1 acionou o Ministério da Saúde para saber se há uma nova previsão de discussão sobre a incorporação, mas não teve retorno até a publicação.

articles.title: Jovem cai de parapeito em bar na Asa Sul e é levado inconsciente ao hospital | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo os bombeiros, vítima tinha suspeita de traumatismo cranioencefálico. Caso aconteceu no Âmbar, no Setor Bancário Sul neste sábado (31).
articles.summary: Segundo os bombeiros, vítima tinha suspeita de traumatismo cranioencefálico e sofreu parada cardiorrespiratória. Caso aconteceu no Âmbar, no Setor Bancário Sul neste sábado (31).
articles.body:
Âmbar em Brasília — Foto: Redes Sociais/reprodução

Um jovem caiu de uma área elevada de um bar no Setor Bancário Sul, na Asa Sul, em Brasília , neste sábado (31). A ocorrência foi atendida pelo Corpo de Bombeiros do Distrito Federal (CBMDF) às 23h52.

Segundo os bombeiros, o jovem estava inconsciente e apresentava suspeita de traumatismo cranioencefálico (TCE). A corporação informou ainda que a vítima sofreu uma parada cardiorrespiratória (PCR).

Após o atendimento, o homem foi transportado pelo Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) para o Hospital de Base. O IgesDF informou que o paciente está internado sob os cuidados da equipe multiprofissional.

Em nota (veja íntegra abaixo) , o Âmbar e a Emopalooza informaram que o estabelecimento não abrirá neste domingo (1º) em razão do ocorrido. As equipes disseram que acompanham a situação e que, neste momento, a prioridade é prestar solidariedade à pessoa envolvida e aos familiares, preservando a privacidade deles.

Uma pessoa que estava no local durante o fato contou ao g1 que havia um parapeito na área onde ocorreu a queda e que não viu nenhuma estrutura adicional de contenção ou bloqueio no local. Segundo o relato, o espaço estava cheio no momento do episódio.

Ainda de acordo com a testemunha, após a queda, o local onde aconteceu o acidente foi isolado com divisórias, mas a festa não foi interrompida.

A pessoa afirmou ainda que viu a vítima recebendo atendimento e sendo imobilizada com um colar cervical, mas disse não saber as circunstâncias da queda.

"Âmbar e a Emopalooza informam que, em razão do acidente ocorrido na madrugada deste domingo (1º de novembro), o Âmbar não abrirá suas portas hoje. O evento Criolina, previsto para esta data, será realizado na @e.x.t.e.r.n.a .

Neste momento, nossa prioridade é o respeito e a solidariedade à pessoa envolvida e aos seus familiares. As equipes do Âmbar e da Emopalooza seguem acompanhando a situação com atenção e sensibilidade, preservando a privacidade dos envolvidos.

As informações sobre o novo local e o horário serão enviadas por e-mail a quem comprou ingresso e divulgadas nas redes do @sistemacriolina . Quem não puder comparecer ao novo local poderá solicitar o reembolso diretamente pela plataforma Shotgun.

Em consideração à delicadeza do momento, os comentários desta publicação permanecerão desativados.

Lamentamos profundamente o ocorrido e agradecemos a compreensão do público."

"O IgesDF informou que o paciente está internado no Hospital de Base sob os cuidados da equipe multiprofissional

O Instituto de Gestão Estratégica de Saúde do Distrito Federal (IgesDF) informa que o paciente mencionado na reportagem deu entrada no Hospital de Base do Distrito Federal (HBDF), na madrugada deste domingo (1º), e recebeu atendimento da equipe de trauma do Pronto-Socorro da unidade.

O paciente permanece internado, sob os cuidados da equipe multiprofissional do hospital.

Em respeito à Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados Pessoais (LGPD) e ao sigilo profissional, o Instituto preserva a privacidade e a confidencialidade das informações clínicas do paciente, incluindo dados sobre seu estado de saúde, tratamentos e procedimentos realizados.

O IgesDF reafirma seu compromisso com uma assistência segura, acolhedora e de qualidade, pautada pelo respeito à dignidade e à privacidade dos pacientes e de seus familiares."

articles.title: Médico é assaltado durante o plantão em UPA do litoral de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Dois homens armados invadiram a unidade de saúde durante a madrugada e renderam uma profissional de enfermagem para chegar até o médico. Segundo a vítima, os suspeitos exigiram que ele desbloqueasse o celular antes de fugir.
articles.summary: Dois homens armados invadiram a unidade de saúde durante a madrugada e renderam uma profissional de enfermagem para chegar até o médico.
articles.body:
Médico foi assaltado na UPA Perequê após esfaquear o marido, em Guarujá — Foto: Prefeitura de Guarujá

Um médico foi assaltado enquanto estava de plantão em uma Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA), em Guarujá , no litoral de São Paulo. Dois homens armados invadiram a unidade durante a madrugada deste domingo (1º) e roubaram o celular, o relógio e uma pulseira de ouro do profissional .

O crime aconteceu na UPA Perequê. Segundo o médico, que preferiu não se identificar, os suspeitos usavam máscaras e luvas, sendo que um deles estava armado com uma pistola.

Conforme apurado pelo g1 , os suspeitos renderam uma profissional de enfermagem logo na entrada da unidade e exigiram que ela os levasse até o médico. Em seguida, foram até o local onde ele descansava durante o plantão.

Além de levar os pertences, os suspeitos exigiram que o profissional desbloqueasse o celular antes de fugir. O caso foi registrado como roubo e será investigado pela Polícia Civil.

O g1 entrou em contato com a Secretaria de Segurança Pública de São Paulo (SSP-SP), mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Em nota, a Prefeitura de Guarujá informou que a segurança da UPA Perequê foi reforçada pela Guarda Civil Municipal (GCM), com o objetivo de preservar a integridade de pacientes e profissionais.

Ainda segundo a administração municipal, o atendimento na unidade segue normalmente.

articles.title: Nadador é atropelado por embarcação no litoral de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Homem foi resgatado pelo Grupamento de Bombeiros Marítimo (GBMar) neste domingo (1º). Segundo o Hospital Santo Amaro, ele passou por cirurgia e permanece com estado de saúde estável.
articles.summary: Se acordo com o Grupamento de Bombeiros Marítimo (GBMar), o condutor da embarcação fugiu sem prestar socorro.
articles.body:
Nadador é atropelado por embarcação no Canal de Bertioga — Foto: Carlos Abelha/TV Tribuna

Um nadador ficou ferido após ser atropelado por uma embarcação neste domingo (1º), no Canal de Bertioga , no litoral de São Paulo. De acordo com o Grupamento de Bombeiros Marítimo (GBMar), o condutor fugiu sem prestar socorro.

A vítima foi resgatada pela equipe do GBMar e encaminhada ao Hospital de Bertioga, sendo posteriormente transferida ao Hospital Santo Amaro (HSA). Segundo o HSA, o paciente deu entrada com uma fratura exposta na perna esquerda. Ele passou por cirurgia e permanece em estado estável.

Em nota, o GBMar informou que o nadador não conseguiu identificar a embarcação que o atingiu. O nome da vítima não havia sido divulgado oficialmente até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Em nota, o GBMar afirmou que condutores de embarcações devem manter uma distância segura de banhistas e nadadores, respeitar as normas de navegação e os limites de velocidade para prevenir acidentes e preservar vidas.

articles.title: Criança de 3 anos morre atropelada em rodovia de Manacapuru, no AM | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo apuração da Rede Amazônica, o motorista parou para prestar socorro e levou a criança ao Hospital Geral de Manacapuru. De acordo com a unidade de saúde, a menina já chegou ao hospital sem vida.
articles.summary: Uma criança de 3 anos morreu atropelada em Manacapuru após tentar atravessar a rodovia AM-352. O motorista prestou socorro, mas a vítima chegou sem vida ao hospital.
articles.body:
Carro envolvido no atropelamento da criança — Foto: Divulgação

Uma menina de 3 anos, que não teve a identidade divulgada, morreu após ser atropelada por um carro na noite de sábado (31), no Ramal Vale da Bênção, no km 25 da rodovia AM-352, em Manacapuru , no interior do Amazonas. Ela estava a caminho da igreja com a família quando tentou atravessar a via e foi atingida pelo veículo.

Segundo apuração da Rede Amazônica , o motorista parou para prestar socorro e levou a criança ao Hospital Geral de Manacapuru (HGM). De acordo com a unidade de saúde, a menina já chegou ao hospital sem vida.

Após o acidente, o condutor foi à Delegacia Interativa de Polícia (DIP) de Manacapuru para prestar esclarecimentos. O corpo da criança foi levado ao Instituto Médico Legal (IML).

A Polícia Civil do Amazonas (PC-AM) investiga as circunstâncias do atropelamento.

articles.title: Gaza doctors struggle with bereavement, overwork, trauma amid genocidal war
articles.summary: Doctors and nurses struggle to cope with the horrors they endured during the height of the Gaza war.
articles.body:
Deir el-Balah, Gaza – Manar Fayyad, 29, an anaesthesiologist at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital , has suffered severe psychological trauma since the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023.

The turning point came when he discovered that a man lying before him in the operating room was his own brother Shadi, who was killed in an Israeli air strike on December 27, 2023.

He recalled the moment he was summoned into the operating room to administer anaesthesia to a critically injured man before emergency surgery.

“He died before I could reach him,” he said. “When I arrived in the operating room, I recognised the man’s clothes. I had a strange feeling, so I approached him and uncovered his face. To my shock, he was my brother Shadi, who was 34.”

Since then, the hospital has become inseparable from the traumatic memory, and he has been unable to continue to work, ultimately bringing his professional career to a premature end.

He continues to struggle with the psychological effects of the experience, trying to cope with it on his own without professional help. He has withdrawn from social life and avoids people and noise as he searches for peace since his brother died.

Sitting by the sea and writing offers him some solace, helping him express his pain and process what has happened. Yet he remains preoccupied with the idea of leaving Gaza, hoping that distance might free him from the reminders of that day.

Having lost his brother, his profession and much of his social life, Fayyad now faces a different battle: one against trauma that he is trying to confront alone.

Khaled Raafat, 29, a nurse in the emergency department at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital, stepped away from work for an extended period after losing his wife, children, mother and several siblings in an Israeli air strike on his family home on October 18, 2023. He was at the hospital at the time, trying to save their lives of others injured that day.

“Learning that I had lost my family marked a painful turning point in my life,” Khaled told Al Jazeera. “I could no longer do my job in the same way. The hospital, once associated in my mind with my humanitarian duty, became a reminder of personal pain that was beyond what I could bear. It deeply affected my ability to continue my professional and social life.”

Raafat said he eventually decided to rebuild his life.

“I realised that life could not stop at the tragedy and that I had to find a way to carry on. I decided to work towards my psychological recovery, got married and started a new family in an attempt to regain stability and hope,” he said. “I then returned to work at the hospital.”

At least 1,700 medical personnel have been killed in Israeli attacks during the war while 83 healthcare workers remain in Israeli detention, according to Gaza’s Government Media Office.

These figures do not reveal the deep psychological burden borne by medical workers who have lost family, friends and colleagues and witnessed horrific injuries and death on a daily basis. They have also faced continued displacement, relentless pressure and have been overworked for years.

A study found that 41 percent reported losing family members and 46 percent had experienced both personal bereavement and displacement from their workplaces, according to a report on the strain on medical workers in Gaza published in the Public Library of Science .

At least 78 percent of healthcare workers in Gaza lacked access to mental health services, showing the gap between the trauma healthcare workers endure and their access to psychological care. It has meant that Gaza’s health system is struggling to retain its remaining staff and prevent them from leaving the medical field.

Although it is difficult to assess how many doctors, nurses and other medical workers have left Gaza and their jobs, official reports have acknowledged a “loss of human resources” and “diminished capacity in the healthcare system”.

To help halt this brain drain and protect healthcare workers who have experienced psychological trauma – probably most of those in Gaza, they need psychological and social support.

“They are caught between their professional duty to save lives and the pain of losing the people closest to them,” Munir al-Bursh, director general of Gaza’s Ministry of Health, told Al Jazeera. “They find themselves treating others’ wounds while struggling to heal their own.”

Working under constant pressure without adequate support or rest deepens exhaustion and threatens healthcare workers’ ability to continue, he said.

“Protecting medical personnel is not just about securing medicines and equipment. It also means safeguarding their mental health and giving them time to rest and recover. Those who save others also need someone to reach out and help them.”

The acute shortage of medical staff after the killings, detentions and injuries of many healthcare workers makes it difficult to give those who remain enough time to recover, he added. This is compounded by the continuing arrival of patients and wounded people, shortages of equipment and a lack of replacement staff.

The experiences of these doctors and nurses reveal the psychological toll of war on Gaza’s healthcare system. Those accustomed to confronting death and saving the wounded have sometimes found themselves facing it as bereaved family members rather than medical professionals. Caught between their duty to save others and their own grief, some have paid a profound psychological price with consequences for both their professional and personal lives.

Nurse Hiba al-Tawil, 39, witnessed her brother’s death in the intensive care unit at the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, where she worked.

“Losing my brother at my workplace was a difficult experience that had a profound psychological impact on me,” she told Al Jazeera. “Being in the intensive care unit afterwards reminded me of what had happened and made it harder to cope with the loss.”

She later transferred to another department. which helped ease the psychological pressure she was experiencing and allowed her to distance herself from the place where her brother died.

The psychological clinic at the hospital treats doctors and nurses struggling with trauma caused by bereavement and their experiences during the war. In some cases, these experiences can develop into severe psychological disorders that affect their everyday lives and ability to work.

Reham Abu Rokba, a psychologist at the complex, said treatment begins with assessing the patient’s psychological condition, diagnosing symptoms and determining their impact before developing a treatment plan.

For patients with post-traumatic stress disorder, treatment may include cognitive behavioural therapy, which helps them understand their psychological responses to traumatic events and regain their ability to cope.

Depending on the patient’s needs, treatment may involve about 12 individual sessions and, when necessary, medication.

Reham said that continued psychological support, appropriate treatment and adherence to the treatment plan can help ease symptoms and lead to improvements.

“Recovery requires time and ongoing participation in psychological support sessions,” she told Al Jazeera. “Providing the appropriate treatment and ensuring adherence to it can help alleviate symptoms and lead to tangible improvements in an individual’s mental wellbeing.”

articles.title: At least eight Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza
articles.summary: Four-year-old among eight Palestinians killed in Israeli drone attacks across the Gaza Strip.
articles.body:
At least eight Palestinians, including a four-year-old boy, have been killed by the Israeli military in Gaza, hospital sources told Al Jazeera.

An Israeli drone attack killed five Palestinian police officers and wounded several people in al-Mawasi, west of Khan Younis, in southern Gaza on Sunday.

Israeli forces had targeted a number of police officers while they were “performing their routine duties”, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Interior and National Security.

The ministry condemned the “horrific massacre” and called on the international community “to take urgent action and exert pressure” on Israel to stop its killing of policemen.

It said in a statement at least 75 police officers and security personnel have been killed by Israel since the “ceasefire” with Hamas came into effect in October last year.

The Israeli army meanwhile claimed that its attack was targeting “a terrorist” in southern Gaza.

Separately, in northern Gaza, at least three Palestinians, including a four-year-old boy, were killed in a drone attack on Gaza City’s Rimal neighbourhood, sources at al-Shifa Hospital said. The Taj Mall was also targeted.

Another person died on Sunday from wounds sustained during a previous attack.

“It’s hard to remember a day gone by when we haven’t reported on deadly attacks across the Gaza Strip,” said Al Jazeera’s Hani Mahmoud, reporting from Gaza City.

“In the last couple of hours, a group of law enforcement officers patrolling al-Mawasi … to protect displaced civilians was targeted. Five policemen were killed instantly.

“An hour on from that attack … in the heart of Gaza City, three people were reported killed – including a father and his three-year-old son – who were walking down Revolution Street,” he said, adding that Israeli attacks have not stopped despite the so-called “ceasefire” in place for more than a year.

Hamas on Sunday condemned the latest Israeli attacks as a “deliberate war crime”.

In a statement, it denounced the “horrific massacre” that targeted a group of police officers as well as the “bombardment of Gaza City” that killed and wounded civilians.

The deliberate and repeated targeting of police officers while they perform their duties is part of Israel’s “attempt to obstruct recovery efforts, undermine stability in the Gaza Strip, and sow chaos”, the statement said, adding that “international silence and the failure to confront these horrific crimes only embolden the occupation”.

“This is yet another chapter in the ongoing series of Zionist atrocities against our Palestinian people … a continuation of the genocidal war whose tragic unfolding our people are still enduring,” Hamas said.

Israeli forces continue to attack Gaza, despite a US-brokered “ceasefire” taking effect last October, killing more than 1,500 people since then.

At least 74,594 Palestinians have been killed since Israel launched its genocidal war in October 2023, in response to the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, according to the Gaza Ministry of Health.

articles.title: 5 habits that could help keep you out of a nursing home, from an orthopedic surgeon
articles.summary: Dr. Vonda Wright shares five daily habits that help older adults maintain independent living, starting with skeletal longevity and muscle strength.
articles.body: Three in four Americans aged 50 and older would like to remain in their homes as they age, according to the AARP — and preserving that independence starts with daily habits. Dr. Vonda Wright, a double board-certified orthopedic surgeon, author and authority on active aging and mobility, who is based in Orlando, Florida, said there are three main problems that can make it difficult for older adults to age in place. Those include difficulty getting up from a chair and caring for themselves, memory problems, and incontinence that makes it hard to manage personal hygiene. FORGET THE GYM: A 30-SECOND TEST MAY BE ONE OF THE BEST INDICATORS OF LONGEVITY "The missing piece in most conversations between mental health, physical health and independence is your skeletal longevity," Wright said. Staying independent with age requires attention to the entire musculoskeletal system, including the muscles, bones and tendons, according to the surgeon. Wright shared the following habits as most important for maintaining independence outside of a nursing home. No. 1: Keep moving The human body "craves mobility," Wright said. "When you think about it, it's our first skill. We learn to walk when we're 1," she pointed out. WEEKLY WEIGHTLIFTING SWEET SPOT MAY BE LINKED TO LONGER LIFE, STUDY FINDS For older adults, staying active can help preserve the ability to handle everyday tasks independently. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention suggests low-impact activities such as walking, cycling and water exercise. "Even when your hips hurt, even when your knees hurt, you should move on the ground, or get in a pool in chest-high water," Wright suggested. While the doctor does not recommend exercising through a new injury or severe pain, she pushed back against the belief that rest is the best way to address pain. PEOPLE LIVING PAST 100 IN ONE TINY VILLAGE SHARE 3 DAILY HABITS "Rest doesn't cure anything. When you have, for instance, arthritic knees, do you know what can help? Building the muscles around your knees, building the muscles in your hips to support your knees," she said. "So rest is not the answer for feeling better — staying strong and mobile is." No. 2: Build muscle Strength training can help older adults maintain the ability to get out of a chair, climb stairs and carry groceries — everyday tasks that support independent living. There is never an age or skill level when it’s too late to build muscle, according to Wright. FITNESS EXPERT REVEALS 6 THINGS PEOPLE OVER 35 SHOULD DO AFTER WORKOUTS TO STAY STRONG "Even if you feel like you've declined or your parents have declined, there is no age or skill level when we can't become more mobile, when we can't build muscle or reconnect the neuromuscular pathways," she said. It’s even possible to build muscle sitting in a wheelchair, she noted. "Some of the very first research done by Dr. Maria Fiatarone at Tufts University showed that even at 90 years old, you can regain function." "There is no age or skill level when we can't become more mobile, when we can't build muscle." In that small 1990 study, nine nursing home residents who completed eight weeks of high-intensity resistance training increased their muscle strength by an average of 174%, and also showed improvements in muscle size and mobility. The National Institute on Aging recommends that older adults perform muscle-strengthening activities at least two days a week, targeting all major muscle groups, with recovery time between sessions. Some options include resistance bands, hand weights and body-weight exercises. Beginners are advised to start gradually and seek guidance from a doctor or physical therapist as needed. No. 3: Eat enough to support strength Older adults tend to eat less, which can undermine efforts to maintain energy and build muscle, Wright warned. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "It’s something I see even happening to my 86-year-old parents; they're just eating less and less," she said. "And we cannot fuel the muscle we want to build [and] the energy we need without a protein-forward, adequate-calorie diet." "The most common mistake I see seniors making as they age is assuming that aging is an inevitable decline from vitality to frailty." Although older adults may require fewer calories, they still need enough nutrients to support their health, according to the National Institute on Aging. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER To help maintain muscle, the agency recommends that older adults consume protein-rich foods throughout the day, including seafood, dairy, fortified soy products, beans and lentils. Specific calorie needs will vary based on each person’s weight and activity level. No. 4: Drop the mindset that decline is inevitable Wright urged older adults to challenge assumptions about what they can and can’t do as they age. "The most common mistake I see seniors making as they age is assuming that aging is an inevitable decline from vitality to frailty," she said. "They just assume that a certain number of birthday candles predisposes them to sitting on a couch the rest of their life. The reality is that there is no age or skill level when you're done." No. 5: Have open conversations Wright suggested that people should start working toward future independence during their busy working years. "We need to start thinking about that in our busiest times of life, in our 30s, our 40s, our prime times of working," she said. "It’s part of a long-term, lifetime plan to live where you want to live, with whom you want to live, when you want to live there." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The doctor recommends that adults directly ask their aging parents what assistance they need and to explore available support, including community programs. In many cases, she said, parents do not want to be a burden to their adult children, so they never ask for anything. "I think this is a time for really open, frank conversations," Wright said. "What do you want help with? How can I help you? How could we get help for you if possible?" TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ As an example, Wright said her elderly parents live with her family. When she noticed their meals started to suffer while she was traveling, she arranged for support to help them continue managing their lives. "I have half of their meals delivered every week because I'm not going to be home to shop or cook," she said. "They remain independent, but with assistance. And that's what works for us."

articles.title: Radiologists warn cancer patients 'deteriorating' amid staff shortages
articles.summary: North and west Wales have a 42% shortfall in consultant radiologists, compared to 22% in south Wales.
articles.body:
Cancer patients have warned delays in scans could be the difference between life and death as Wales faces a shortage of radiologists.

The Royal College of Radiologists said NHS Wales currently had 88 fewer radiologists than it needed - a 28% shortfall.

For the first time, it has reported seeing some patients' conditions "deteriorating" while waiting for diagnostic scans and tests.

Radiologists are doctors who specialise in using images to diagnose and manage medical conditions and diseases.

Betsi Cadwaladr health board, which covers one of the areas most affected by shortages, said recruitment was ongoing and, despite a substantial increase in demand for scans, reporting times had improved.

Beverly Scott, who was first diagnosed with ovarian and peritoneal cancer 14 years ago, said treatment was keeping her condition stable but without timely scans it was at risk of spreading unnoticed.

Scott, who is a member of Pwllheli and Pen Llŷn cancer support group in Gwynedd, was given five years to live when she was first diagnosed.

She took part in medical trials at the Royal Marsden Hospital in London and said that while there was no cure, continual treatment was now keeping her cancer stable.

Scott said the shortage of radiologists could threaten this stability.

"For the past 14 years, I have lived with scans," she said.

"In cases like mine, delays could cause the cancer to spread further and treatments wouldn't work."

Another member of the group, Karen Jones, was first diagnosed with breast cancer in 2015. She was subsequently diagnosed with colon cancer, and her breast cancer also returned in 2021.

She said: "Waiting for results is the worst part, will it be clear or not?

"It is terrible, horrific and horrendous. You are in total limbo."

North and west Wales are among the areas worst affected by shortages in the UK, with a 42% shortfall in consultant radiologists compared to 22% in south Wales, according to data published in the Royal College of Radiologists' 2025 clinical radiology census.

Clara Day, executive medical director at Betsi Cadwaladr health board in north Wales, said she understood the figures "can be very worrying for patients", adding the health board was "actively recruiting" into both radiology and oncology - the department which handles cancer diagnoses and treatment.

"We are also strengthening our links with the North Wales Medical School to support future workforce development."

She said the health board's clinical strategy for oncology had led to "key developments", including nurse-led clinics and the introduction of colorectal and breast metastatic nurse specialist teams.

"Robust arrangements are in place to maintain safe services, prioritise patients according to clinical need and to continue delivering high-quality oncology care for the people of north Wales," she said.

Day added that "despite a substantial increase in demand for imaging services", partnering with a third-party provider had contributed to a decline in waiting times for scans and results since April.

She said these reporting times were also closely and consistently monitored.

One of the main reasons for the shortage is that Wales has more radiology departments affected by recruitment freezes than anywhere in the UK.

In 2024, the radiology workforce in Wales grew by just 1.1%, far below the UK average of 5%.

Dr Owen Nicholas, a consultant oncologist in Swansea and chair of the Welsh committee for the Royal College of Radiologists, said: "It is not getting better and the patients are now getting affected."

He said the shortage was also impacting staff, adding: "There is a challenge, where you sit in front of a patient who is extremely anxious to know has the treatment worked or has it come back.

"For you to have to say, 'sorry I don't know, because I don't have the report in front of me', or perhaps you cancel an appointment because a scan report has not come back.

"The primary concern is for the patient, but it is not very nice for a clinician to have to do that over and over again."

articles.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
articles.summary: Five officers from the Hamas-run police have been killed in Khan Younis and three people, including a child, killed in Gaza City, officials say.
articles.body:
Israeli strikes in Gaza have killed at least eight people, including a child, according to hospitals, despite a year-old ceasefire.

In Gaza City to the north, hospital officials said a missile attack hit a group of civilians next to Cairo School in the Al-Rimal neighbourhood, killing three people, including a four-year-old boy.

In the southern city of Khan Younis, the Hamas-run ministry of interior said a drone attack targeted a group of police officers in the Al-Mawasi area, killing five, as they were carrying out their routine duties.

The Israeli military said it had carried out two attacks on what it described as military operatives but has not yet provided evidence or further information.

Outside Gaza City's Shifa Hospital, video showed a crowd of men gathered to pray next to two body bags and the tiny body of the child, which was wrapped in a white towel.

"My son and his child were martyred. They were sitting in their tent, bothering no one, and nothing else was happening in the area when suddenly, a missile struck them, and they were martyred," Ali Oweis told AFP news agency. "There is no ceasefire; the war is ongoing, don't you see?"

At Nasser hospital in Khan Younis, women despaired as body bags lay on the floor, video showed. The interior ministry named the five police officers killed, who were between the ages of 23 and 53, and called the attack a "horrific massacre".

A ceasefire came into force in Gaza in October last year, but Israeli air strikes have continued almost every day.

Since then, 1,580 people have been killed, according to Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. Israel says it is targeting Hamas, but often civilians are also killed.

Meanwhile, a peace plan for Gaza, brokered by the Trump administration, has stalled.

The ceasefire saw thousands of Palestinians held by Israel released in return for all of the 48 remaining hostages held in Gaza, and an agreement to end the war.

The conflict was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage.

Since the war began, 74,594 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the territory's health ministry.

articles.title: Paz Padilla y sus consejos sobre el duelo: "Que haya pasado un año no significa que le quieras menos"
articles.standfirst: Así lo mencionó en una entrevista en 'El Hormiguero'
articles.summary: Así lo mencionó en una entrevista en 'El Hormiguero'
articles.body: En un día como hoy, muchas personas, asisten a visitar a sus seres queridos que han fallecido o les tienen un recuerdo y cariño especial para tenerles en mente y seguir teniéndoles en sus recuerdos y pensamientos. Lo cierto es que el duelo es uno de los momentos más complejos de entender y de gestionar para una persona. No solo por la desaparición de alguien que ha formado parte de nuestras vidas, sino también por la falta de comprensión de un proceso tan natural como inexplicable como lo es la muerte. Paz Padilla, quien ha atravesado una pérdida muy relevante, contó en una entrevista en 'El Hormiguero', cómo fue lidiar con ello y qué es lo que aprendió de esta situación inevitable. Puede parecer que la trascendencia de un ser querido puede ser lo más duro y, aunque es terrible, lo peor viene en muchos casos una vez ya se ha dado esta situación. Volver a casa y ver que ahí no va a estar más el ser querido, no recibir sus llamadas o ver la ropa y objetos personales de la persona que ya no está con nosotros en el plano físico. El duelo es difícil y, aún más, cuando tienes que empezar a desprenderte de estos objetos. Según Padilla, los profesionales te aconsejan que cuando empieces a darte cuenta de que esa persona ya no está, es bueno desprenderte de esas cosas para comenzar el duelo. Tal y como menciona la actriz, humorista y presentadora, "le ponemos una carga emocional a un trapo" pero la persona que perdemos no es una prenda de ropa. Es posible que, las fechas, sean otro de los momentos cruciales y en los que peor se pase. El primer aniversario de su fallecimiento, las navidades o su cumpleaños, suelen ser momentos en los que nos aferramos aún más a su recuerdo. Paz Padilla mencionó lo que le costaba a ella esta clase de fechas y estos momentos concretos y cómo tuvieron que lidiar con estos momentos. Esto sucede porque nos ponemos en la fecha y no solo recordamos, sino que revivimos todo lo que hemos pasado en esa fecha. Y es que, cada vez que recuerdas y lo ligas a lo que ha sucedido puedes pasarlo mal pero no es real, aunque la sensación regrese. Por ello, tenemos que "aprender que es un día más, como el de ayer, porque el que haya pasado un año no significa que tú lo quieras menos o que tu dolor o pesar sea diferente."

articles.title: Al Jazeera marks 30 years of transforming news in Middle East and beyond
articles.summary: The anniversary coincides with a significant restructuring of Al Jazeera Media Network’s Arabic-language news services.
articles.body:
Doha, Qatar – As Al Jazeera marks its 30th anniversary with a special commemorative event, the media network’s history is a timeline of milestones and challenges – from risks, obstacles and attacks, to international awards and recognition from the communities whose stories it strives to tell.

Launched on November 1, 1996, the network broke new ground in Arab broadcasting, bringing previously marginalised political perspectives into the mainstream and creating space for debate on issues seldom openly discussed on regional television.

On Sunday, the network hosted an event to commemorate its enduring legacy at its headquarters in the Qatari capital, Doha, attended by the Emir of Qatar Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and other delegates.

Since its launch, Al Jazeera was not “just a screen”, said Al Jazeera’s Director General Sheikh Nasser bin Faisal Al Thani at the anniversary event. “It was a promise that journalism can be free and responsible, and that ‘opinion and the other opinion’ is not just a slogan, but it’s a position you take.”

For three decades, Al Jazeera “has helped transform the way news is covered in the Arab world”, Director of News Raed Fakih said in a statement, hailing the network for making room for “voices, issues and perspectives that had not been given the space they deserved”.

“Today, as we mark Al Jazeera’s 30th anniversary, we are building on that editorial legacy to broaden the scope of our coverage and give greater prominence to a wider range of events and viewpoints,” he added.

The anniversary coincides with a significant restructuring of Al Jazeera Media Network’s Arabic-language news services, separating rolling breaking news coverage, live event broadcasting, and more in-depth reporting across three channels.

Since Qatar’s late Father Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani launched the independent channel – a first in the Arab world – the network has promised to provide “the opinion and the other opinion”.

It launched its first TV broadcast as an Arabic-language satellite news channel in 1996 from Doha and has since then grown into the Al Jazeera Media Network, with several outlets in multiple languages. A private corporation for public benefit, the network now includes television channels, websites and other digital platforms.

But as governments have banned it, and as its offices have been bombed in many parts of the world, the network has exacted a huge cost for staying on air.

Yet it has been instrumental in covering key events in the last three decades in the region and beyond.

In 2001, when the United States attacked Afghanistan, Al Jazeera was the only foreign broadcaster in Kabul, its updates and pictures travelling the world.

Then in 2011, millions followed the Arab Spring uprising live on Al Jazeera. Its coverage won a prestigious Peabody Award.

However, the network’s reporting has led to numerous threats over the years. Exclusive pictures have made Al Jazeera hard to ignore, but have also made the network a target.

In 2003, a US strike hit its Baghdad office, killing correspondent Tareq Ayyoub. Two dozen Al Jazeera journalists have been killed since.

In 2022, an Israeli soldier shot Palestinian correspondent Shireen Abu Akleh in Jenin, the 12th Al Jazeera journalist killed in 19 years. Another 12 were then killed in just 30 months, every one of them by Israel during its genocidal war in Gaza.

One of them was Anas al-Sharif , who for many viewers was the face of the war. In August 2025, an Israeli strike killed him and four colleagues as it hit a press tent outside al-Shifa Hospital.

“To the martyrs of Al Jazeera, to our colleagues who departed while carrying out their duties, we say to them today, you are part and parcel of Al Jazeera’s promise,” Al Jazeera’s Sheikh Nasser said at the event on Sunday.

Meanwhile, across the region, governments have closed the network’s bureaus and pulled the channel’s licences.

In 2024, Israel banned the network and raided its Ramallah office. Months later, the Palestinian Authority suspended it.

Overall, at least nine governments have tried to silence Al Jazeera.

Despite the challenges, Al Jazeera’s broadcast continues, with more than 3,000 staff working out of more than 70 bureaus across the globe.

Alongside its digital divisions, as well as its English channel that launched in 2006, Al Jazeera reaches more than 430 million homes.

The network on Sunday also launched The Core, an artificial intelligence (AI) initiative first announced in December 2025 in collaboration with Google Cloud. The initiative aims to integrate AI into newsroom operations, helping journalists manage information, coordinate coverage and make better use of the network’s reporting archives.

Meanwhile, Al Jazeera Balkans was also relaunched in a new digital-first format, opening a new chapter in its journalism in the region.

While the network’s shelves are packed with hundreds of awards, it continues its mission of serving as a voice of the voiceless.

articles.title: Cops bust Rajkot bigwigs’ liquor party, 38 booked under Prohibition Act
articles.summary: Rajkot police raided a Kalavad Road banquet hall liquor party, booking 38 under Gujarat Prohibition Act; bottles seized, staff probed, more names possible.
articles.body: Rajkot: A birthday party-cum-pre-Diwali bash attended by prominent industrialists, builders, jewellers, financiers and doctors from Rajkot and Morbi ended in a police raid late on Saturday night, with 38 people booked under the Gujarat Prohibition Act for drinking liquor. The gathering, hosted at Saraza Banquet Hall on Kalavad Road, was reportedly organised as an early birthday celebration for a prominent businessman.The Local Crime Branch (LCB), acting on a tip-off, raided the venue around 11 pm on Oct 31. The operation continued until 4 am on Sunday. Guests were subjected to breathalyser tests, while blood samples were collected at the civil hospital to establish whether they had consumed alcohol.Some attendees reportedly attempted to shield their identities from media cameras by covering their faces with tablecloths while being taken for medical tests.DCP Zone-2 Rakesh Desai told TOI that the raid was conducted by a team led by PSI Shaktisinh Chudasama after receiving information about liquor being served openly at the banquet hall.Preliminary investigations revealed that the party was organised by a prominent builder who had reportedly planned an advance birthday celebration combined with a pre-Diwali get-together.As many as 76 people, including family members and spouses, were attending the party. The guest list included prominent builders, industrialists, financiers, jewellers, doctors and people associated with the tours and travels industry from Rajkot and Morbi.Those present included a vitrified tiles businessman who is reportedly related to a politician.Serving staff also under scannerThe investigation also indicated that some members of the banquet hall’s serving staff had allegedly consumed alcohol while serving guests. Three of them, along with the hotel manager, were named in the police complaint.While preliminary breathalyser tests indicated that most male guests had consumed alcohol, women present were initially found not to have done so. However, police collected blood samples from everyone for confirmation. Additional names may be included if laboratory reports establish alcohol consumption, said police.Liquor bottles seizedRajkot taluka police registered a case against 38 people, including the organiser, under Sections 65(A)(A), 66(1)(B), 75A, 83, 86 and 116-B of the Gujarat Prohibition Act. Empty and foreign liquor bottles worth approximately Rs 17,500 were seized from the venue. All 38 accused were served notices and subsequently released. ACP South Division B J Chaudhary said the notice process was completed by 4 pm on Sunday.Banquet hall 850m from police stationAdding another twist to the case, Saraza Banquet Hall is barely 850m from Rajkot taluka police station. articles.title: Women's sex drive treatment linked to higher rates of heart attack and stroke
articles.summary: A study of 6,000+ postmenopausal women links testosterone therapy to higher rates of heart attack, stroke and heart failure in new research.
articles.body: Postmenopausal women who use testosterone therapy could face a higher risk of heart attack, stroke and other cardiovascular problems, new research suggests. The research, presented at the 2026 annual meeting of The Menopause Society last month in San Diego, looked at more than 6,000 postmenopausal women age 45 and older, comparing those who received testosterone therapy with those who did not. Women with a history of cardiovascular disease were excluded. Among women receiving testosterone, 3.8% experienced a first-time cardiovascular event compared with 0.5% of women who were not receiving the treatment, according to The Menopause Society. POPULAR ARTIFICIAL SWEETENER LINKED TO POTENTIALLY DANGEROUS HEART RISK Those events included heart attack, stroke, heart failure and other cardiovascular problems. Testosterone is a sex hormone produced by the ovaries and adrenal glands that plays a role in sexual desire, as well as muscle and bone health, mood and cognition, according to Cleveland Clinic. Anna Cabeca, a Dallas-based board-certified OB-GYN and menopause expert, told Fox News Digital that the differences between the two groups — women who received testosterone and those who did not — deserve attention. "The difference between 3.8% and 0.5% is certainly significant enough to warrant attention, but we need to be careful about what these numbers actually tell us," said Cabeca, who was not involved in the study. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES That amounts to about 38 cardiovascular events per 1,000 women receiving testosterone compared with five per 1,000 women who were not, the doctor noted. For women considering testosterone therapy, Cabeca said doctors should look at the patient's overall health, including heart history, blood pressure, cholesterol, metabolic health, medications and family history. "Sexual health is an essential part of overall health, and women deserve to have their concerns about libido, arousal and intimacy taken seriously, particularly during and after menopause," she added. While testosterone can improve sexual desire and satisfaction in appropriately selected postmenopausal women, the possible benefits should be weighed against potential risks, Cabeca advised. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER In cases when testosterone is appropriate, she favors careful dosing, monitoring and regular checks of a patient's symptoms and lab results. There are important limitations to the new findings, the researchers acknowledged. The study was observational, meaning the researchers looked at outcomes among women who were already receiving testosterone rather than assigning the treatment in a controlled trial. As a result, the study can show a link between testosterone use and cardiovascular events, but cannot prove that the treatment caused them. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Women who received testosterone may also have differed from those who did not in ways that affected their heart risk, including age, blood pressure, diabetes, cholesterol levels or other health factors, Cabeca said. "This is an important safety signal that deserves further investigation, not definitive evidence of causation," she added. articles.title: Sen. Chris Murphy hospitalized after suffering a stroke, chief of staff says
articles.summary: "We are optimistic he will make a full recovery," Murphy's chief of staff said.
articles.body:
U.S. Sen. Chris Murphy has been hospitalized after suffering a stroke, his chief of staff said in a statement on Sunday.

The 53-year-old Democrat was taken to a hospital on Saturday after he started to feel numbness in his arm while attending his son's hockey game, said Allison Herwitt, Murphy's chief of staff.

Upon examining Murphy, doctors determined he had suffered a stroke, Herwitt said, adding that the senator has been transferred to Johns Hopkins Hospital in Baltimore.

"The doctors are encouraged by his progress, he is awake and alert, and we are optimistic he will make a full recovery," Herwitt said.

No further information was released about Murphy's condition.

For the past several weeks, Murphy has been traveling the country campaigning for Democratic candidates in Tuesday's midterm elections. He was scheduled to appear Sunday with Democratic Senate candidate Chris Pappas in New Hampshire, according to the New Hampshire Democratic Party.

In 2024, Murphy won his third term to serve Connecticut in the U.S. Senate and has been viewed by some Democratic party officials as a possible candidate for president in 2028.

Connecticut Gov. Ned Lamont released a statement on social media on Sunday saying he and his wife, Annie, are keeping Murphy and is family "in our prayers."

"Just two days ago, I was with Senator Chris Murphy doing what he loves most: Encouraging Connecticut residents to make their voices heard and vote on Tuesday," Lamont said. "There is no stronger advocate for our democracy. And no one who fights harder for the people of this state. Chris is a great friend to Connecticut and to me personally."

"I am sure that he will be walking across the state again very soon. And we will all be cheering him on," Lamont added.

articles.title: Your walking speed may hold a clue to how long you’ll live, study suggests
articles.summary: A JAMA Network Open study of over 4,000 older adults found faster walking pace was linked to lower death risk over nearly 12 years of follow-up.
articles.body: The speed a person normally walks could offer a simple clue about their overall health and longevity, new research suggests. A study published in JAMA Network Open followed 4,067 adults in the U.K., who were about 69 years old on average, to see whether their usual walking pace was linked to their risk of death over time. Participants completed a short walking test at their normal pace and also wore a wrist activity tracker for nine days to capture their walking speed during everyday life. FORGET THE GYM: A 30-SECOND TEST MAY BE ONE OF THE BEST INDICATORS OF LONGEVITY Over nearly 12 years of follow-up, faster walking in both settings was linked to a lower risk of death, even after researchers accounted for other health and lifestyle factors. A total of 739 participants died during that period. Beth Templin, a board-certified geriatric clinical specialist and CEO of HouseFit Physical Therapy & Fitness in St. Louis, said walking speed can offer a broader look at how well the body is functioning. "In physical therapy, we call walking speed the 'sixth vital sign' because it's a snapshot of how well many body systems are working together," Templin, who was not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Changes in walking speed can therefore offer clues about a person's health, according to the doctor. "To walk briskly, you need strong legs, a healthy heart and lungs, good balance, and a brain and nervous system that can coordinate it all," she said. "When walking speed starts to slip, it's often an early warning sign that one of those systems is declining, sometimes before anything shows up on a lab test," Templin added. For older adults who want to improve their walking speed and overall fitness, simply taking more steps may not be enough. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "Build the engine, not just the habit," Templin advised. "Most people try to walk more, but speed comes from strength and balance." The doctor suggested strengthening the legs with simple exercises, such as standing up from a chair without using the hands and doing heel raises while holding onto a counter. She also recommended adding short bursts of faster walking. After warming up, a person could walk briskly for one minute, slow down for two minutes and then repeat, gradually increasing the faster periods. The findings do not mean that simply walking faster will make someone live longer, experts noted. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "This study shows an association, not proof that walking faster by itself adds years," Templin reiterated. The participants included in the study were generally healthier than the larger group, the researchers noted. There is also no single standard method for measuring everyday walking pace with wrist activity trackers. More research is needed to determine whether the findings apply to other groups.
